attribution: Miya.m — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Aso caldera floor and the central volcanic cones seen from the rim
caption: The Aso caldera, one of the largest on Earth, with the central cones rising from its floor. Day 6 drives the rim and crosses the caldera floor to reach it.

attribution: TANAKA Juuyoh — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Columnar basalt cliffs and the river in Takachiho Gorge
caption: Vertical basalt walls above the river in Takachiho Gorge, Miyazaki. Day 7 visits the gorge and the shrine, where night kagura is performed.

attribution: At by At — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Sakurajima volcano above the Yunohira observation deck, with the viewpoint sign in the foreground
caption: The bare, ash-streaked slopes of Sakurajima seen from the Yunohira viewpoint, at 373 m on the volcano's flank. This is the safe-distance stop of Day 9, after the short ferry from Kagoshima.

attribution: 江戸村のとくぞう — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Wooden ryokan buildings along the stream at Kurokawa Onsen
caption: Wooden bathhouses and ryokan lining the stream at Kurokawa Onsen in Kumamoto. Day 5 ends here with the three-bath pass at dusk and a night in a ryokan or minshuku.

alt: Steaming blue hot-spring pond at Umi Jigoku in Beppu
caption: Umi Jigoku, the sea-blue boiling pond of the Kannawa hells in Beppu. It is the first sightseeing stop of Day 3, on the hot-spring coast.

commonsFile: File:Stone Niō Statues, Futago-ji temple, Kunisaki - Mar 19, 2024.jpg
attribution: Bruno Rijsman — CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Stone Niō guardian statues at the entrance of Futago-ji temple
caption: Stone Niō guardians at Futago-ji, a mountain temple on the Kunisaki Peninsula. It opens Day 4's rural temple loop, along with Fuki-ji and the rock-carved Buddhas of Kumano.

alt: Kumamoto Castle keep above its sloping stone walls
caption: The Kumamoto Castle keep and its curved stone ramparts, one of Japan's largest castles. It is the main stop of Day 10, reached by Shinkansen from Kagoshima.

commonsFile: File:View of the Former Dutch Trading Post on Dejima from Tamae Bridge, Nagasaki, 20240815 1459 3716.jpg
attribution: Jakub Hałun — CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: The restored Dutch trading post on Dejima seen from Tamae Bridge in Nagasaki
caption: Restored warehouses on Dejima, the artificial island where Dutch traders were confined during Japan's closed period. It is the reason to include Nagasaki on Day 12.

alt: Open volcanic highland of the Ebino Plateau in the Kirishima range
caption: The Ebino Plateau in the Kirishima range, a volcanic highland of crater lakes and scrub. Day 8 is spent walking and driving here.

attribution: Hide1228 — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Kusasenri grassland in winter below the Aso volcanoes
caption: Kusasenri, the grass plateau at the foot of Mount Nakadake, in its winter state. It is the stop on Day 6 just after the caldera rim, and shows what February looks like in Aso.

attribution: Yoshikazu TAKADA from Tokyo, Japan — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Open-air yatai food stalls lined along the Nakasu riverside in Fukuoka
caption: Hakata's yatai street stalls at Nakasu, lit in the evening. This is the setting of the first yatai dinner on Day 2.

commonsFile: File:Manai Waterfall 真名井の滝(まないのたき) (3430044721).jpg
photographer: TANAKA Juuyoh (田中十洋) from Japan
attribution: TANAKA Juuyoh (田中十洋) from Japan — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Manai Falls dropping into the river of Takachiho Gorge
caption: Manai Falls in Takachiho Gorge, the waterfall that rowing boats pass beneath. It is the daytime highlight of Day 7, before the evening kagura.

commonsFile: File:140321 Shimabara Castle Shimabara Nagasaki pref Japan01bs5.jpg
alt: Shimabara Castle with its white keep and stone walls
caption: Shimabara Castle, rebuilt on the Shimabara peninsula below Unzen. It is a stop on Day 11, after the ferry from Kumamoto Port.

location: Kagoshima Bay, between Kagoshima and Sakurajima
alt: A Sakurajima ferry crossing Kagoshima Bay
caption: One of the frequent ferries across Kagoshima Bay. The short crossing to Sakurajima is the Day 9 signature experience, before the car return.
